summary: A short memo from the Network Working Group chair urging sites to set real schedules for finishing their software. Each site's liaison was asked to give dates for implementing the Host-Host protocol as changed by RFC 107, plus Telnet programs for users and servers. John Heafner at Rand agreed to track progress and test implementations.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo asks network sites to set dates for finishing their NCP and Telnet software and related documentation. John Heafner will monitor progress, test the implementations and collect reports of unclear protocol rules.

sections.title: A Request for Firm Schedules
sections.content:
Steve Crocker says it is time to set serious schedules for implementing NCPs and Telnets. John Heafner of Rand agrees to monitor each site's progress and test its implementation.

Each Network Liaison Contact is responsible for preparing a schedule and sending it to Heafner.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site must prepare a schedule for its network software. John Heafner will track progress and test what each site builds.

sections.title: What Each Schedule Must Include
sections.content:
The schedule must give dates for implementing an NCP under Document 1 as modified by RFC 107, a user-Telnet for logging in to other hosts, and a server-Telnet for allowing remote users to log in.

It must also give dates for documenting how to connect and log in, how to obtain job numbers and passwords, what services the host offers, and when it will operate regularly during advertised hours.
sections.plainLanguage: The schedule covers software, instructions for users and regular service hours. It must include dates for each of these items.

sections.title: Monitoring and Protocol Questions
sections.content:
Heafner is responsible for prompting host teams to produce schedules, software and documentation. He will test advertised implementations and investigate reasons for delays.

The memo also names him as the person to contact about ambiguities, gaps and misunderstandings in the protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: Heafner will check that sites meet their schedules and test their software. Sites can also report unclear or insufficient protocol rules to him.

references.text: RFC 107, which modifies the specifications for the NCP implementation schedule.
